title: What Would You Ask an Animal?
summary: If you could talk to any animal, which one would you choose? The idea might sound like something from Dr. Dolittle, but scientists are making real progress toward understanding how other species communicate. Researchers recently used artificial intelligence to decode segments of birdsong. At the University of California, Berkeley, ethologist Julie Elie used AI and behavioral experiments to work out what zebra finches are saying to each other. She could tell which calls the birds use to communicate over short distances and which ones they use over longer distances. Birds are not the only animals scientists hope to understand. Researchers with Project CETI are using AI to decipher the clicks and calls of sperm whales. Meanwhile, a separate team working with the search for extraterrestrial intelligence, known as SETI, carried out what they described as the first conversation between humans and a humpback whale. The whale, named Twain, responded to recorded calls played by the researchers over 20 minutes. Scientists believe the exchange could one day help us figure out how to communicate with life from other planets. Closer to home, cats have already figured out how to use meows to get our attention, whether they are demanding food, affection or simply asking us to open the door for them again. Whether cats truly understand human language is still up for debate. But it raises a fun question. If we could understand what animals are saying, which species would you most want to talk to? A dog, to find out what it really thinks of the mail carrier? A whale, to hear about life in the deep ocean? Or a bird, to ask what it sings about at dawn? The science is still young, but the idea of a real conversation with another species is moving from storybooks into the laboratory.
why_it_matters: Understanding animal calls could change how we see other species and even help us think about talking to life beyond Earth.

Artificial intelligence can now study huge numbers of animal sounds and look for patterns.
